images.title: A circle has no smallest turn
images.purpose: Contrast a square, which has a smallest turn of 90 degrees, with a circle, which fits after any turn.
images.composition: Square on the left and circle on the right, equal in size, wide space between, labels below each.
images.exact_structure: Left: one teal #0072B2 square with a centre dot and a grey #6B7280 quarter turn arrow. Right: one amber #E69F00 circle with a centre dot and a very small grey turn arrow. Exactly 1 square, 1 circle, 2 dots, 2 arrows. No marks on the circle's rim.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a circle drawn with a mark that breaks its sameness
images.takeaway: A circle fits itself after any turn, so it has no smallest angle.
images.description: A teal square with a 90 degree turn arrow beside an amber circle with a tiny turn arrow, showing the circle has no smallest turn.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to say which shape has a smallest turn and why the circle does not.

image_decisions.why: The contrast of square and circle is a picture idea; one clean image carries it.
